newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Four Budapest bombings target car dealerships.
newsitem.headline: Four Budapest bombings target car dealerships.

text.p: Four almost simultaneous bombings shook Budapest early on Thursday, causing damage but injuring no one, police officials said.
"There were four bombings altogether," Etelka Posvancz of Budapest police told Reuters.
She said police had no reports of injuries and at this early stage could not tell the extent of the damage.
The MTI news agency said three of the four bombs exploded in or near used car dealerships, causing extensive damage in at least one location.
The fourth bomb went off in a luxury car, damaging it and other cars around it.
Police experts said the four bombings, all within an hour, were probably a concerted action, Budapest police spokesman Mihaly Desi told Hungarian radio.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in May that police had made a breakthrough in solving the Budapest bombing wave which began last September.
At the time, police said the bombings were aimed at diverting police attention from fuel tax and excise duty evasion amounting to billions of forints.
They had said earlier that the almost two dozen of grenade and petrol bomb explosions, most of them in Budapest, were linked to an escalating gang turf war.
